question: A can lay railway track between two given stations in 19 days and B can do the same job in 11 days. With the help of C, they did the job in 2 days only. Then, C alone can do the job in
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM of 19, 11, and 2 = 418 units.

A's efficiency = 418 ÷ 19 = 22 units/day.

B's efficiency = 418 ÷ 11 = 38 units/day.

(A + B + C)'s efficiency = 418 ÷ 2 = 209 units/day.

C's efficiency = 209 − (22 + 38) = 149 units/day.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ¹²⁰⁄₁₄₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Time taken by A = 19 days

⇒ Time taken by B = 11 days

⇒ Time taken by A, B, and C together = 2 days

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of C = Total Efficiency − (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 209 − (22 + 38)

⇒ Efficiency of C = 209 − 60 = 149 units/day

⇒ Time taken by C alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency of C

⇒ Time taken by C alone = 418 ÷ 149 = 2 ¹²⁰⁄₁₄₉ days

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ¹²⁰⁄₁₄₉ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work Concept

Total work is usually considered as the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of all the given time periods. This makes efficiency calculations easier and avoids complex fractions.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to time taken. Work done = Efficiency × Time. Combined efficiency of a working group is the exact sum of their individual unit-day efficiencies.

Work & Wages

Whenever individuals work together for the complete duration, their total wage distribution happens exactly in the ratio of their daily efficiency rather than the number of days they worked.

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

Conceptually identical to Time & Work problems. Inlet pipes have positive efficiency (filling) while outlet pipes or leaks have negative efficiency (emptying the tank).
